cases.description: empty input survives untouched
a burst of pure whitespace yields nothing
Whisper emits [BLANK_AUDIO] on silence; it must never be delivered
the (blank) artefact variant
the [INAUDIBLE] artefact variant
the [silence] artefact variant
the artefact is matched after stripping, not before
an artefact inside real speech is NOT a whole-burst artefact; dropping the sentence would lose the user's words
a burst starting with punctuation is a decode artefact
leading full stop is stripped
leading ellipsis character is stripped
a run of dots and spaces is stripped
only LEADING punctuation is an artefact; the user's full stop stays
sentence-internal punctuation survives
a burst of nothing but punctuation
only whitespace, dots and ellipsis are stripped — not every mark
already-clean text passes through unchanged (clean_text must be idempotent)
non-ASCII letters are untouched
RTL text must survive byte-for-byte; Persian is a first-class test language for this project
leading-punctuation stripping must not corrupt RTL text
astral-plane characters are untouched
only the ends are trimmed; internal structure is the user's
code identifiers must survive dictation into an editor
two artefact markers back to back are not a match for any single known artefact string, so the exact-match check leaves both alone
artefact matching is case-sensitive; a lowercase variant of the marker slips through untouched
same case-sensitivity gap with a mixed-case variant
extra spaces inside the parenthetical artefact break the exact match
a word before the marker means the burst is no longer whole-artefact, so it is kept — the mirror of the already-covered trailing-word case
a unicode ellipsis immediately followed by an ascii period is still one leading punctuation run
dots separated by spaces are still a punctuation-only burst
two consecutive ellipsis characters are stripped as one leading run
whitespace variety around the marker doesn't stop artefact stripping
leading whitespace and a dot immediately butting against RTL text with no space between them
trailing punctuation after RTL text is untouched, mirroring the ASCII trailing-punctuation rule
a lone emoji survives untouched
leading period stripped, astral-plane emoji stays
no space between the stripped ellipsis and the emoji that follows
a lone dot plus trailing whitespace reduces to nothing
a lone dot plus exactly one trailing space also reduces to nothing
surprising: U+200B is invisible but Python does not consider it whitespace, so it survives strip() and every check untouched

surprising: a leading byte-order-mark is also invisible and also not whitespace, so it breaks the exact-string artefact match — a BOM-prefixed [BLANK_AUDIO] burst is delivered to the user as literal text instead of being stripped
RTL variant of the embedded-marker-is-kept rule
correctness must hold at meeting-length input, not just short bursts — leading punctuation is still stripped and the rest of a long paragraph survives byte-for-byte

cases.description: two different markers glued together with no separator are not a single recognized artefact string and both survive
an embedded marker preceded by real words and a comma is kept, another embedded variant
contrast with zero-width-space-survives: the full-width ideographic space (U+3000) IS Unicode whitespace and is correctly stripped from both ends
contrast with bom-prefixed-marker-not-recognized: a non-breaking space (U+00A0) IS Unicode whitespace, so it's stripped before the exact-match check and the artefact underneath is still recognized
leading decode-artefact dot is stripped even when it's glued directly to a code identifier with no space
a burst mixing Latin, Arabic and CJK script in one string has nothing to strip and survives whole
less common ASCII whitespace controls (vertical tab, form feed) are still whitespace-only
